cands.bio: Republican U.S. representative for Alabama's 6th District since 2015. Before Congress he co-founded and led the Alabama Policy Institute, a conservative think tank, for about 24 to 25 years. He chaired the House Republican Policy Committee from 2019 to 2025. He earned a University of Alabama business degree.

controversies.text: Federal records show $27,900 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $589 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26; 1 trip paid for by the American Israel Education Foundation, AIPAC's affiliate.
Missed 8 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (1.2%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 1, 2025-04-09 to 2025-04-09.

In 2021 U.S. Term Limits announced a billboard saying Palmer broke a pledge to cosponsor a term-limits amendment. His campaign called that false, saying he cosponsored it three terms running. In 2023 Palmer said he had said he'd serve only five terms: "I own that." He announced a run for a sixth term.

endorsements.text: Donald Trump is listed as endorsing Palmer in the 2024 and 2026 election sections.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions by Palmer on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land conservation, police pay and pensions, or school choice and teacher pay. The sources disagree on his birth town. He never held state or local elected office before Congress. Part of the Ballotpedia page was cut off in the 118th Congress key-votes section, so later content on that page was not read.

cands.name: Maurice Mercer

money.note: Individuals gave $22,777; PAC money $5,300; candidate's own money $3,590. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Democratic nominee for Alabama's 6th Congressional District in 2026. Business account executive with a Troy University business degree. Served on the Pelham City Council from 2012 to 2025, including as Council President from 2020 to 2025. Has also worked in telecommunications, banking, retail management, logistics and small business.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists recommendations from several Sway voter-guide groups, including 'Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress' (Vote for Peace) and Tabitha's List. These are informal voter-guide groups rather than organizations.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Maurice Mercer was born or raised, or when he came to Alabama. We found no records of specific Pelham City Council votes, so his council record is known only from his own campaign descriptions. We found no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, gun policy, school vouchers or charters, teacher pay, or limits on development. His campaign platform page was cut off partway through the immigration section, so anything after that was not read. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages reviewed.

score.why: Raised $34.8k, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $34.8k, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Three terms on the Pelham City Council (2012-2025), including Council President 2020-2025. Business account executive for a Fortune 500 company, with past work in telecommunications, banking, retail management, organized labor, logistics and small business ownership.
qual.why: Over a decade of local elected office, including a council presidency, plus business management experience. He has no state or federal legislative service, which puts him in the middle range.
qual.label: Over a decade of local elected office, including a council presidency, plus business management experience. He has no state or federal legislative service, which puts him in the middle range.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says that on the Pelham council he consistently supported police, fire and first responders with resources, tools, training, equipment, recruitment support and disability protections, while also calling for transparency and accountability.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says he supports a woman's right to make her own healthcare decisions. It also says he believes every life has value and favors easier adoption, expanded foster care and support for families. It does not endorse abortion restrictions.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site supports strong border security and enforcement resources, and a fair pathway to legal status and citizenship for long-term residents. It calls for enforcement with due process. The page is cut off in the passage on violent criminals, so his full position on detention is unread.
